NARRATOR: Hear now the song of Troy,
and of the years the sea would not forget.
Long ago, the kingdoms of Greece united
in a common cause...
summoned by oath and honor.
Their kings gathered a mighty fleet
and sailed across the sea to the great city of Troy.
Its walls higher than any siege tower,
thick enough that no battering ram could break them.
A city that should never have fallen.
At its heart was Helen, wife of Menelaus, king of Sparta,
and when the Trojan prince Paris carried her away,
the kingdoms of Greece arose as one.
For ten long years, they lay siege to Troy.
Though countless warriors fought and died,
the city remained unconquered.
But where armies had failed, cunning would prevail.
Under the cover of darkness,
Odysseus set a daring plan into motion.
Greek warriors entered the city unseen.
By dawn, Troy was consumed by fire,
and the long war had come to an end.
Yet for Odysseus, patient as the tide,
and cunning beyond all others,
the longest journey was just beginning.
The King!
King Odysseus!
Our men are gone, but Troy is fallen,
and our battle is won.
Where are we going?
Home. To my kingdom.
To my son. My wife.
You may join me.
Be an advisor in my court.
For your bravery in this terrible war, I will ensure
you will want for nothing for the rest of your life.
Thank you, my King.
It would be my honor.
The journey will not be easy.
I will swim if I must, but I will get home.
Trojans!
If the gods are willing.
Tell me, O Muse, the man of many devices,
who wandered full many ways after he had
sacked the great citadel of Troy.
Home, then.
Lest I have not honored the gods
enough to receive the reward I deserve.
Greetings, Odysseus.
The good man.
Bright-eyed Athena.
Goddess on high.
Clever, maybe.
Clever is better than good.
Not just clever.
Brutal, decisive, and ingenious.
Hiding your soldiers in the gift of a wooden horse,
your Trojan horse.
Taking the city by surprise from the inside out.
Your greatest work.
It did what it was made to do.
But I cannot look behind.
As any craftsman worth his salt, I pray
that my greatest work lies ahead.
Perhaps it does.
So home, then. Ithaca. To your wife.
Your city.
Yes, the only journey worth the fight.
Are you coming with me, Athena?
Or is there another reason for this visit?
I come to bring you a warning.
The gods, they are fickle, Odysseus.
They will not make your journey home an easy one.
Your trials will be their entertainment.
They know now that you are a clever man.
They are jealous.
They will use this against you to show their power.
Curse me or bless me, Goddess on high.
But be quick about it.
In due time.
And so begins your odyssey.
And the game of the gods.
Then pray for me, goddess.
For I must reach home.
For my kingdom.
My everything.
My son. My wife.
My world will be gone.
I am looking for men.
A crew for a dangerous journey.
One the gods themselves may turn their will against.
Once I am home, as king of Ithaca,
I assure you each will receive a suitable reward.
You will never want for anything for the rest of your lives.
You have the word of the king himself.
A generous offer and reward.
But are you as good as your word?
Polites!
You look a little bit past your prime.
- By the gods! - Old man.
After all this time.
All this time and you still haven’t gotten any better
at motivational speeches.
Absolute crickets from you as well.
This is a man who has saved my life on numerous occasions.
A debt we have both repaid each other more than once
in a war that has lasted more than five years.
Although it’s closer to ten now.
But these days,
I am much better collecting scars than I am glory.
But, you will find plenty of much younger,
probably not as bright men more than willing to join you.
But probably not here,
sipping goblets in the middle of the day.
And the rest here,
well, they know not the true cost of war,
though they may be eager.
- As once we were. - As we once were.
Listening to our fathers and our grandfathers stories.
And just more than willing to prove ourselves.
Can I trust them?
About as much as you can trust me.
All I know is that what’s waiting for you back in Ithaca,
now that is your reward.
And you deserve it, too.
But for the rest of us...
Join me. I need men who I can trust.
Men with experience in battle.
No, no, no. I will not be going to any battle.
Or any wars. Ever again.
I am unpersuadable. I cannot be persuaded.
Did I mention the gold?
Well, did I mention unpersuaded?
When do we start?
As soon as we recruit two more.
- Two more? - Yes.
Okay. Let’s go.
Alkimos the Navigator.
From what I heard, he was the one that saved a ship
of fishermen from a cyclone.
Really?
I’ve heard of you, King Odysseus.
What have you heard?
That you, sacker of cities, son of Laertes,
are favored by the gods.
Not all the gods. One or two. Maybe less.
You survived the Trojan War.
You’re a king.
The King of Ithaca.
I have a family that comes from Ithaca.
I haven’t seen them since I was little.
You know, my king--
I’m not king today.
But if you help me get home, I will be.
I’m a good navigator.
But you mentioned gold.
Did I?
Oh. You did. Yes. You mentioned gold.
He mentioned gold.
Hmm.
I don’t seek gold.
I’m bored.
Bored of fishing boats filled with old men
with putrid smelling cargo.
I seek adventure.
New shores.
Like in the stories.
Stories about you.
Then join me,
and we will make stories that they will never forget.
And I promise you, it will be anything but boring.
And once we reach Ithaca, you can join my guard
and help me protect our fair kingdom.
My king.
Now, how are you at fighting?
I can handle my own.
But if you want a force to be reckoned with,
you want to recruit Eurylochus,
I’ve never seen another man fight quite like he has.
We’ll pay him a visit next.
So what say you, Eurylochus?
I have killed a lot of men to protect my home.
War has plagued our country for many years.
How are you at sea?
I’m a fast swimmer, and even faster with a sword.
Hm. Is that so?
Hm.
But now that the war is over,
I’ve found work at a vineyard up the road.
The owner, he treats me well.
And his daughter, Talia, she’s...
I just don’t know if I can commit to a journey this long.
You will be in Ithaca before sundown two days hence.
We have to be.
And if you decide to stay in our fair kingdom,
you will live a life of ease in Ithaca.
And once there, she can join you.
If you teach me how to be as fast
as you, my king Odysseus, then I’m in.
And as I promised...
We need gold.
You said we need to be to Ithaca in two days.
Yes. I have a plan.
But you must trust me.
I’m with you to the end, my king.
Or thereabouts.
From Troy, Odysseus launched his journey home
with 12 ships and 600 men.
Back in Ithaca, Odysseus’s dear wife Penelope
dreams of her love bearing the brutal seas
to find his way home to her.
Odysseus?
God’s above.
You’ve shown me Odysseus lives.
Now bring him home.
Bring him home now, or these lips
shall never again speak your names.
A growing boy needs food.
A boy needs many things, mother, but I am not a boy.
Not any...
Mother.
I’ve seen him, Telemachus.
I’ve seen your father.
You’re bleeding. You must sit.
No, my son. We must stand and fight.
What have you seen?
A vision.
A message from the gods.
Troy burns.
Your father, he is triumphant.
He is coming home, but it may not be fast enough.
Ithaca is vulnerable now.
Now that the war is over,
Odysseus must return to reclaim the throne, otherwise
another can claim this kingdom as his own.
Your father would rather die than let that happen.
He will return. He must.
And in his absence, I am the man of this house,
and I say that we...
You will be a man soon enough, my love. You will.
But you cannot be king. Not yet.
And therein lies our fight.
Each day that your father is away, others become
more willing to claim this kingdom as their own.
If he does not return, I will not also lose you.
So we must be strong, my son.
Together, we must be like your father.
Smart and resourceful.
And protect this kingdom without violence.
Clever.
So clever as to make the gods jealous.
Whether we want it or not, the heavens will continue to
move without Odysseus here by our side where he belongs.
If he does not return soon
after victory has been declared,
then by law he will have abandoned his duties as king.
And a suitor, any suitor,
may lay claim to this house,
and to the crown of Ithaca.
And to you.
The law only reaches so far.
When they come, and come they will,
we must be ready.
And I am ready to fight for you and for father and the kingdom.
Son, this is not going to be a sword fight.
Or even a fight of fists.
This will be a fight of words and propriety.
We need to buy him time.
Keep the suitors busy.
Their bellies full and distracted.
Now come and honor me like you do him.
The war is over now.
But our battle is just beginning.
Goddess Athena...
Help us.
I pray.
But help Odysseus.
Help my father.
Please.
The mighty storm that struck Odysseus
ravaged the sea for ten days, taking them far off course.
After battling the sea,
Odysseus has arrived at his home in Ithaca...
or so he thought.
This is not Ithaca, Athena!
This is another one of the gods’ cruel jokes.
I must get home.
I will get home.
Penelope.
Sweet Penelope.
I will come home.
Look at you keeping step with the gods.
Athena.
I am many leagues off course.
I’m only two days journey from Ithaca.
Please.
Spirit me home to Ithaca, great goddess.
You know that I cannot.
It is not within my power to do so.
But think, Odysseus.
Perhaps there is a reason that you are not yet home.
The gods have another plan.
I see.
I am here to help.
I can offer you help three times along your journey.
Three gifts.
Only three?
’Tis all I am permitted.
I am helping because I see myself
in your clever mind and your tactician’s brain.
Your glory in the Trojan War honors me.
And that is why I will help you.
I am flattered, goddess.
I must decline.
I am offended.
Odysseus. Refusing a gift from the gods?
From Athena herself.
If you cannot spirit me home then please
understand I must ask for help only when I need it.
When all hope is lost, my wits abandon me and death beckons.
In this moment I will honor your generosity
for I know the value of godly gifts.
Then you must know even now
dogs are sniffing at your house
and at your wife.
The gods are testing your cleverness, Odysseus.
Then I pray the gods do not stall me
any longer than they already have.
Go, hero.
Honor me and prove your worth.
Get home.
No matter what horrors the gods place upon your path.
The opportunity here is too great to pass up.
A kingdom, a crown,
and even the queen herself
all free for the taking.
And it should be easy enough owing to propriety
and Grecian law.
All suitors must be taken seriously.
And I will be the first.
Ha!
The early bird gets the kingdom.
She’ll have no choice but to honor my demands.
All of my demands.
Antinous just said the most awful things.
Threatening to take the crown, our house, and you!
Then it has begun.
We must be on our guard, Telemachus.
Always polite and inviting.
But on our guard.
But on our guard!
Perilous winds and unsettling new lands
take their toll on the voyagers
who now explore a small island, rich in gold.
Is this part of the plan, Lord Odysseus?
Indeed, Eurylochus.
Now stay close, and your lips closed.
I don’t quite understand what this has to do with gold.
We’re going to retrieve gold.
My gold that was stolen by a cyclops.
He’s the son of Poseidon, God of the sea.
A real cyclops?
Why didn’t you tell us sooner?
They eat people, so I’ve heard.
My brave crew...
Alkimos, you wanted adventure.
Here it is.
Eurylochus, you wanted to stay alive in a cave with a Cyclops.
You must learn to be faster.
And Polites, now you wanted gold.
Yes, this cyclops has been hoarding gold for years.
Mine and others.
And that gold will help me pay your rewards.
He’s been terrorizing this mountainside for many years.
It’s time we return the favor.
Today, our journey begins with a cyclops.
Or it ends before it begins.
Now who’s with me?
My king.
Help! Help!
Help! Help!
He... He ate him.
Do as I say when I say, then we will win the day.
All right, what’s the plan?
We’ll circle the base of the mountain.
Go inside.
Stay close, and downwind.
Cyclops, he can smell us nearly a league away.
Hold, hold, hold.
At Troy, during the war, you were there?
I sure was.
I barely survived, and I probably wouldn’t have
if it weren’t for Odysseus.
Saved me from an entire garrison.
Picked them off one by one.
Hiding in the shadows, which is a pretty big
feat for him, considering he’s a big bastard.
I’ve only heard stories.
Legends, really.
Well, not everything you hear is true.
Only half of what I just said was true.
Is he as good a man as they say?
He’s a great man, though he’d never admit it.
But out of humility.
He’s a man who values many virtues.
But the one he values above all others is cleverness.
You see, a good man engenders himself to friends, family.
A clever man, a clever man survives.
Quickly, now.
Gods willing, we will, too.
Keep your eyes open and your wits about you, man.
Odysseus, you know no-ones actually entered
the Cyclops cave and lived to tell the tale.
Not until today they don’t.
He will be busy with his guest.
This is our chance.
We sneak in, find the treasure,
take what we can carry, stay quiet,
get out the same way.
Stay with me.
Stay low.
But how do we find the treasure?
Where does the cyclops even keep its treasure?
It smells like death.
What better place to hide your gold than in
a place that smells so bad that no one dares enter?
Use your nose. Follow its direction.
Is... Is somebody here?
I smell... I smell men.
I smell your fear.
You can’t... You can’t hide for long
and Polyphemus, the son of Poseidon,
is still hungry.
There.
The smell of the worst is that way.
Move, move.
Let’s move.
Quiet.
Holy gold.
Reward.
Rewards for good men.
Shh.
Okay, quickly.
Take everything you can.
Actually, only what you can carry, just like Odysseus said.
Wait, where is Odysseus?
Odysseus is gone.
You’ve come for my gold!
Shh!
- Thieves! - Okay, take cover!
Thieves, who are you?
We’re nobody!
Grab the treasure! Run!
Go! I’ll keep him busy!
We fight with you, my king!
Eurylochus!
Odysseus!
Polites, help! Ah!
No! No!
You will die, foul beast!
For Eurylochus!
Nobody?
It calls for help.
No one will come!
It calls out for nobody.
No one will come.
May the gods bless you, Eurylochus,
and speed you through the underworld
as quickly as the gods will permit.
Now, go. Grab the treasure.
The son of Poseidon will not lick his wounds long.
Go!
- Only take what we need. - Only take what we need.
Yes, enough for a boat.
Provisions and no more.
Okay, here’s a bit of gold. There’s a bit of this...
- Hurry! - Yes, grab that.
That’s expensive, I like that. Okay, and...
Yes, let’s go.
Go, go!
Charie!
And greetings to the great house of Odysseus.
Greetings to you, traveler.
Your voice seems so...
familiar.
But our house is in no condition...
Aye, aye. Well met, my lord Telelachus.
Telemachus.
Apologies. Apologies.
I am Antinous.
And I come bearing gifts.
The gift of my protection.
A gracious home.
A kingly estate, indeed.
Ready our ship, men. We leave port immediately.
- My king. - My king.
Come to wish us farewell?
I have.
And I come bearing a gift.
A bag of wind to speed you along your journey.
Perhaps if you’d accepted my offer of help,
and asked for stronger and faster ships,
you would not need it.
Or you would already be closer to home.
My ship.
I would not trust a boat from the gods.
Who knows if the previous owners seek revenge and come find me?
And what of the previous owners of this treasure?
My ship.
My treasure.
My men.
What’s left of them.
By Olympus.
One of the gods speaking to Odysseus.
Gifts.
Gifts from the gods themselves.
It’s a generous gift.
And I accept your bag of wind.
But it is not one of your three gifts until I use it.
Why not use it now?
I will use it.
But I will use it when I must.
The gifts of a god come with a heavy price.
Hurry home, son of Laertes.
Honor me.
Rewards.
Odysseus!
Was that...
Athena herself.
Come to wish us a farewell.
Could she help us?
Help us get there faster.
I would give my life many times over if it
meant getting home sooner to my loved ones.
But the gods play dangerous games with men.
They could spirit us home with just a mere thought.
Or the breath from their lungs.
Or they could smite us where we stand and send us to our dooms.
To them, it’s all the same.
That’s why we must tread lightly.
Especially with the ones who seem the most generous.
And what of that?
Is that a gift? A reward?
No, it’s nothing.
It’s a good luck charm.
Now, Polites, let’s go home.
A guest in my home.
Aye, but not just any guest.
Antinous, my queen.
At your service.
Well met, Antinous.
And to what do we owe this generous visit?
I come to pay my respects to the great Odysseus himself.
And to those he left behind.
He will return. He...
And we accept that respect
in the spirit that it was given.
Thank you, Antinous.
And I am here to confirm that this home is safe.

And to offer my allegiance and my duty to you
and yours and to this kingdom.
And to offer my services to you
as husband and father...
and king.
There is no need for that.
Or for you. My father--
You’ll forgive my son.
He can be rather spirited.
Much like his father.
A generous proposal, indeed.
But we have only just met.
Perhaps we can get better acquainted first.
A fair suggestion.
Right and good.
But I have to admit, my gracious queen.
I am famished.
And my lips are parched from my long journey to your door.
Yes. Refreshments might do us all some good.
Telemachus.
I could use your help.
Take your time.
Take your time.
I’m in no rush.

My duty, my son.
And I expect you to do the same.
Antinous is our guest.

It’s just like I warned you.

Peace is kept.

It is all we can do.
For now.
Now, come on.

My king.

Keep it steady, Alkimos.

Poseidon’s bad breath.

She can’t hold it.
She will do what we tell her to do.
The wind going one way and the current the other.

If we catch the wind, tread lightly.
We can crest the waves instead of wrestling with them.
Yes.
We must tread lightly if we want to keep pace with those.
Spit all you want, Poseidon! I will not be swayed.
Not today, not ever.
Odysseus...
The waves!
The waves, they’re coming right for us.
We’ve got to keep her on course!
Try harder.
Come on! Come on, oh gods. Punish me!
Punish me!
The sea, she means to turn us over!
- Odysseus. - Hold tight.
Hold tight, men. We can steer her.
We’re not strong enough.
We’re not going to make it.
The sea shall eat us all.
The wind. The wind’s too strong.
We’re going to lose the sail.
No. No, it’s not too strong. It’s the strength we need.
Hand me those lines.
Pull the oar. Pull with all your might!
Pull!
If we lose the oar, we’re done for.
If we do not act now, we die.
Pull the oar!
Pull it!
That’s it. That’s it!
The wind is the strength we need.
It’s working.
Odysseus.
Wind.
Wind and water.
They are nothing.
They are nothing when Ithaca waits for us.
I’m coming home.
I am coming home.
So then...
Queen Penelope.
Antinous.
Do you have need of more food?
Or drink perhaps?
Both. Please.
Your wine.
It has a lovely bouquet.
A noble vintage indeed.
A captivating aroma.
And sweet acidity.
It is rich.
And full bodied.
Just like you.
You do flatter me, Antinous.
Maybe I do.
But...
I worry...
The time for flattery has passed.
There will be other suitors
lining up at your door.
And soon...
They will be much less patient men than I.
And after the suitors
will come the looters.
And then the troublemakers.
And I will be unable to protect you.
Unless?
Unless I am your husband.
Unless I am king.
I would hate to see anything unfortunate befall you...
Or your son in such
rudderless times as these.
It is time to make your choice, Penelope.
Before someone makes it for you.
Alkimos, get some beeswax.
Focus repairs on the prow of the ship.
That storm really took a bite out of our hide.
But we need the ship to have her speed back.
Yes, my king.
The sea herself added another day and a half to our journey
that we do not have to spare.
The woes of my heart upon this sea.
What storm do you think was worse?
The one we just sailed through, or the one that is on your brow?
The storm to come.
The journey ahead.
The journey home.
Yes.
Polites, is I must get home no matter what the cost.
I must.
I wonder if the costs already paid.
No, Polites...
The costs were paid both here and back in Troy.
With flesh and blood.
And this. This is our reward, is it?
More hardship.
More storms. Rough seas.
I cannot control the fates. Nor the seas.
You forget that I’ve seen you
perform miracles before, Odysseus.
Miracles even the gods couldn’t choose.
If this was my kingdom, yes.
But this is not my kingdom.
Back home in my kingdom--
By the gods of the sea!
The sea has teeth!
By the gods!
Charybdis!
It’s another one of Poseidon’s weapons of vengeance.
You didn’t stop Poseidon.
You just made him more angry.
Alkimos, come steer.
Steer us around the outside of it.
My king, the repairs aren’t finished yet.
Without them, we won’t be able to make that turn.
It will be almost impossible.
I will make that turn. I will.
The sea!
It has swallowed so many,
but I had no idea it had a mouth!
My king, the winds!
We’re losing speed!
Odysseus, what do we do?
We will not let it dissuade us off our course.
Push, Alkimos!
Push, Polites!
Push!
We will ride the wind and the waves to freedom!
Aye, my king!
Odysseus!
Look!
By the gods! It follows!
Use the gift, son of Laertes! The gift!
The gift the goddess gave to you!
If it can help us, use it!
Soon, loyal Polites!
Use it now!
I will not let Poseidon’s pet beat us.
He will not have the glory of knowing I took the easy way out.
Move!
He is right.
You should use it.
It is too early in the game for you to die, Odysseus.
Your pride will be your ruin.
You cannot win this without help.
I can beat this beast on my own.
I do not need your help, goddess.
I will get home in spite of you...
and all the gods!
I will waste no more breath on you.
Not when it can be used for another purpose.
My king...
Who the hell is it you’re talking to back there?
I will beat this beast without your help, goddess.
The whirlpool!
It’s coming!
Better hold on to something.
Hold on, men.
It’s not just any whirlpool.
It’s a creature of Poseidon.
And if it’s hungry, we must feed it.
We must feed it until its belly is full.
Until it chokes!
Come on!
What do you mean feed it? Feed it with what?
Quick! Or we’ve already lost.
Yes, what the storm has taken from us.
Grab the ropes.
Anything, planks, barrels.
Grab anything you can.
Absolute madness. You went mad, old man.
Feed this beast. Fill its belly.
And if not...
I will choke it myself with my own body.
Looks like the sea must eat.
The fishing traps.
Yes, the provisions. Now!
The fishing traps? What are we going to eat?
We don’t need them.
We’ll be home in two days.
Or we’ll be dead trying to protect it.
Choke on it!
Choke on all of it!
It’s working! It’s working!
Now what we need is distance. Move!
Hear me, gods!
I am strong enough to fight my own battles.
Damn you! Damn you!
Gods.
Please, please help us.
Father...
Father, why have you abandoned us?
Odysseus is alive.
Who... who are you?
Save your breath, child.
Do not fear me.
How have you appeared like that?
Is this some magician’s trick?
A phantasm?
Please do not vex me, spirit!
Athena hears your prayers.
And you must hear my words.
Your father has not abandoned you.
And neither have the gods.
I am doing all that I can.
Never before have I seen a man fight for his home
so boldly as your father does in war.
He honors me.
And for that, I am doing all that I can.
But now, my child, I must ask the same of you.
You must protect your father’s house
at all costs, from within and from without.
You must be prepared to fight in war, yes.
But you must also be careful, watchful, and cunning.
It is time for boys to become men.
I see Odysseus in you.
Perhaps it will be enough.
Yes.
Perhaps it will be enough.
Be vigilant, Telemachus.
You will know it when the moment comes.
And then you will strike...
for your mother, for your father, and for me.
A toast, then.
A toast to our health,
and in gratitude to my most gracious hosts.
Who, if I might speak freely,
deserve a king who would protect them at home,
and not seek glory elsewhere.
And I most certainly could be that king.
A kingdom so fine deserves a ruler
who would never think to abandon it.
This is the king’s house.
Odysseus’s house.
My father’s house.
Ah.
And where exactly is your father, Telemachus?
I don’t see him.
All I see instead is a home deserted,
a kingdom undefended, vulnerable,
and of the king himself some stories.
The poets are talking out on the street.
Some say he’s lost at sea.
Others, that he dallies with Cersei herself.
And I myself have heard nothing but stories of
monsters and treasure
and violence and such bloodshed.
Whatever stories you’ve heard, you should know this:
while my father is gone and in his absence,
I am bound to defend what is his.
Well, if it’s a fight you’re looking for, boy.
Honorable Antinous.
Strong words do harm to the digestion.
And violence is an ill guest in this house or any.
Please.
Of course, my lady.
Of course.
But I wouldn’t need to be a guest if my queen
would take this suitor to be her husband.
I fear I cannot remarry.
What?
I cannot remarry until I finish this cloak
I’ve been making for my son.
It is only custom and proper.
A parting gift for my only flesh and blood.
Before my duties as queen to my new king
fill my days and my hand.
Indeed.
Now far be it from me to rush propriety.
And I surely look forward to viewing the finished product.
Must the entire sea move against Odysseus, Lord Poseidon?
Behavior from such a god seems small and petty.
This isn’t petty.
This is revenge!
For my son, for what Odysseus did to my son.
Your son, Lord Poseidon, was harming and murdering innocents.
Perhaps he will think twice next time.
Enjoy your pet hero while you can, Athena.
With your gifts.
Your meddling matters not.
Odysseus will not leave my ocean alive.
Polites, how is she?
Is she patched up yet?
She’s looking pretty good.
Pretty good, a little bit more...
beeswax and she’ll be good to go.
Good, good.
Set a course for home, Alkimos.
Yes, my king.
For home, and for our rewards.
Gold.
Yes, yes, indeed, Polites. Indeed.
And just on that, by the way, I’ve been meaning
to tell you, meaning to ask about...
Odysseus!
A monster!
The Scylla! Poseidon’s lap dog!
Alkimos, no!
Odysseus!
What do we do?
We try to outrun it.
The wind...
The wind will guide us.
Yes... Yes, faster!
Faster!
No!
No! There’s not enough wind at our back!
Not enough wind to fight!
Only the monster at our heels!
Damn my pride!
Athena! Athena!
I’m asking for help!
Another gift, then?
Goddess! We need weapons!
Ask, and it will be yours.
Strategy. And sight.
Sight.
That will be my second gift.
To see what is right in front of you.
What is right in front of me?
What? What does that mean?
My ship.
You ask for a weapon, and yet you sail one.
Yes.
Why didn’t I see that before?
The ship is a weapon.
Sometimes you are so worried about what is ahead,
that you fail to see what is directly in front of you.
Take heed, Odysseus.
You will defeat the monsters that surround you.
Odysseus?
Odysseus, you’re steering us...
You steer us right towards it!
Right towards the jaws of the beast!
Not the jaws! It’s belly!
We’ll run it through with the prow!
The ship will be our sword!
Yes! Yes!
Odysseus, it’s not going to work!
We’ve got to turn her around or we’re done for!
The current is too strong!
It’s not working!
She’s going to eat us alive!
Hold fast, Polites!
We need momentum!
I’m trying!
That’s the only belly-full you’ll get today!
Yes, Odysseus!
Yes!
Come on, Telemachus.
You must be ready to fight!
Or we’ll lose everything.
Come home, father. Quickly.
The cloak you make for me is nearly finished.
And there are unwanted guests in your house.
About the cloak...
Alas, my son.
I fear there is still so much work to be done.
This cloak may take many days to finish.
You’re undoing what you’ve done.
If only I could.
Mother, you’ve done nothing wrong.
It’s just...
What?
Undoing the cloak every night.
Sometimes clever is better than good.
I just pray it buys us the time he needs.
And if it doesn’t, then I will be ready to fight.
No one is taking this kingdom from us.
No one.
And I will be ready to fight.
Odysseus?
Odysseus.
Treacherous waters ahead.
♪ Come to us
That’s treacherous waters indeed.
It means we’re getting close to land now.
Huh.
That’s the first good thing I’ve heard all day.
We must stay clear of those rocks.
And I have less than a day before...
Yeah, before someone claims what is rightfully yours.
I know, my king. I know.
I am no king here.
There is only one king in the ocean.
And I hold no favor with him now.
♪ Come to us
Odysseus...
Can you hear that?
- Music? - No.
No, not the songs...
of the sirens, no.
♪ Come to us
No.
Polites, no. No!
Protect yourself!
No!
- Sirens. - Not the sirens!
They call to me.
No!
Cover your ears!
Protect yourself, Polites!
They speak to me.
Cover your ears! Protect yourself!
They want me to get my reward.
Rewards for a good man.
No. No!
They speak to me.
I hear the song. It’s in my head!
They speak to me.
Telemachus is the real problem here.
The woman? I can handle.
But the boy?
Any loyal dog would struggle obeying a new master.
And I wouldn’t blame him.
But once this is all mine,
he will still be a thorn in my side.
And his mother falling into line won’t help.
No.
He’s going to require a far stronger hand.
It’s not a matter of if.
Simply put, the question becomes do I take care
of Telemachus now, or do I take care of him later?
It’s like my father used to say.
Only a fool leaves today’s jobs until tomorrow.
Well, Antinous is no fool.
Neither will this loyal dog.
No.
This loyal dog will be ready for you, Antinous.
My reward...
Speak to me.
Odysseus! I need to get my rewards!
What? What are you doing?
My rewards, my gold! They’re speaking to me!
- Not when we’re so close! - Yes!
No! Just pass the rocks, and we’re nearly home!
They speak to me!
Polites! Polites!
Wake up!
Take this beeswax!
Put it in your ears!
We must block their song!
We must block the siren’s song!
Block it!
We cannot hear them!
We’ve got to stay clear of them!
We’ve got to stay away!
Steady on the course...
until we can’t hear them!
Steer away...
Steer away.
That song... That song...
Oh...
I want to hear that song.
Odysseus!
- That song... - Odysseus!
Odysseus! Don’t listen to them!
Here!
No, the wax!
The wax!
The song...
Odysseus! We’re leaving! We’re getting out of here!
I want to hear that song.
They know nothing but death!
- They want to help us. - They do not.
- They do want to help us. - They don’t want to help us.
- Polites... - Think of your family!
- Polites, they want to help us. - No, no, no!
They will not!
Polites, they know how to get home.
We’ve come this far!
- Polites... - We’ve come this far!
- They only know death! - They have wisdom!
They only know death!
Their song is wisdom.
Hey! Snap out of it!
They want to help us.
They know what lies beneath the waves.
I must hear this song.
Song of the sirens.
What a beautiful song.
Huh.
They want to help us get home.
They do.
They have knowledge.
Polites, they have wisdom.
- Odysseus... - Their beautiful song.
I must hear it.
Odysseus, they know nothing but death.
They have knowledge.
They know nothing but death.
Think of home.
The song.
No, Polites, we must steer towards them.
Polites, they want to help us!
No, they don’t!
Yes! Their song!
I want to hear their song...
Please, Polites. They sing for me!
Odysseus!
Odysseus! Hear me, Odysseus!
You must not listen to them, Odysseus!
I can only hear their song.
Odysseus!
No!
You can’t hear me over their song!
Odysseus!
You will die if you don’t make it past these rocks!
And if you cannot hear me, I cannot help you!
I cannot help you.
Odysseus!
Odysseus, no!
Polites, we must steer away from the rocks.
Please steer away from them.
We must get to Ithaca.
They will give us a hero’s welcome.
A king’s welcome.
Damn the sirens.
And damn these seas, too.
Polites, please forgive me.
You have saved both of our lives.
It was an honor, my king.
But now our course is set.
You are almost home.
And that is your reward.
But mind, my king, my reward is treasure.
You must listen to me. You don’t understand.
No, no, no, I do understand.
You have a gift from the gods.
And Ithaca, now that is your reward.
Now I am in pursuit of mine.
You said, your words.
What do you mean?
Gifts for good men. Did you not?
Please, you do not understand.
No, I do understand. It’s you that doesn’t understand.
I saw Athena herself give it to you.
- I saw her. - No, no.
A gift from the gods. Reward.
No, it’s not a gift.
- Oh, it’s not a gift? - No, it’s not.
I see it.
I see, clever Polites, loyal Polites,
worthy of scars Polites,
but not worthy of a gift from the gods, is that it?
Please listen to me. Please listen to me.
Exactly like Troy, is it?
Exactly like Troy.
I am going to take what is owed to me.
For good men.
No, no, do not take that. Do not take that!
Bring it back. You do not understand.
- No, stop. - I do understand.
Stop! Polites, please, please.
My King, I am only opening this
because this is what is owed to me.
- No. - Yes.
Athena.
Athena, please.
Perhaps the fates are more generous than we thought.
Athena.
Even the winds had mercy on you and brought you home.
Reward. Reward.
Great Odysseus finally returned to the shores of Ithaca.
Ithaca.
Telemachus... Penelope!
The great Odysseus...
At the end of his ropes.
No.
Not yet. Not quite.
Look.
There, Your Majesty.
Your people are in panic.
Perhaps there is no more glory left for you here.
Penelope and Telemachus are doing all they can.
But your city is being taken by force.
My world burns.
And the gods abandon me with my hands tied.
I can offer no more aid, and you know this.
By breathing wind into your sails,
strategizing your boat as a weapon,
and giving you a bag of wind,
your three gifts have been used.
But great goddess, I never opened the bag of winds.
It was Polites. Polites opened the bag of winds.
Not I.
A wrinkle.
Perhaps it is enough for the gods to allow me
to aid you one last time on your journey.
I have one boon. One gift left.
I just pray I don’t have to use it.
Yes, but you cannot just go home, Odysseus.
Not anymore.
The people of Ithaca, they are a mob.
They run through the streets hungry for blood.
They would have yours.
You will not make it past them.
You will not even make it to your front door.
And if you did, the suitors would be waiting for you.
In disguise.
In disguise to hide my face in my own kingdom.
I shall dress as a wandering beggar
and learn how things stand.
What will you do, Great Odysseus?
I will defend my home.
My family.
I must stop this before it’s too late.
Or even if it’s as you say,
there’s no glory left for either of us.
Finish the game, Odysseus.
And finish it well.
For not all gods have abandoned you.
And Poseidon still thirsts for revenge.
We must do something, Mother.
No.
I will not let them kill you.
You must get control of the city.
We will wait until your father returns.
Rioting!
Looting and violence,
and you want to wait for Odysseus to return?
Do you still think you’ll have a kingdom by then?
Without a king, my queen,
the city succumbs to its more primal urges.
I will take your hand and the crown with it.
And all will be well when King Antinous reigns.
It is time, my lord.
Time enough indeed for the final challenge.
No more games, loyal widow.
Being king is no game.
And only the worthy wear our crown
and complete this final task.
Only our king can fire an arrow through those axe blades.
And only our king has done it.
So are you our king, Antinous?
Or does Odysseus, even in his absence, carry the crown?
You’re not worth of such a great feat!
I challenge you for my Father’s kingdom!
Snake in the grass!
Stay in your place, pup!
Telemachus!
But if I must, I will teach you to keep your place!
The crown will never be yours!
Snake in the grass!
Interloper! Villain!
Yes, I am.
And much worse.
Begging your apologies.
I was merely returning the young man his sword.
I would like to ask the young lady if I may compete.
Another suitor?
With the queen’s permission, of course.
We need no more suitors!
I will--
The courtesy of my husband’s house
is much diminished as of late.
You may compete.
And I pray you might restore what has been lost.
Only Odysseus can put an arrow through those axe blades.
So, let’s see how good you are.
Good.
Clever.
Clever is better than good.
It’s a farce!
He can’t even keep the arrow straight, my queen.
Best keep your eye on the target, old man.
So, only Odysseus himself can make this shot.
And I must be Odysseus.
But Odysseus is dead!
- No! - Father!
You have overstayed your welcome in my house too long!
Antinous!
You can leave on your own accord.
Never!
This kingdom is mine!
Or you can go another way!
Death is too good for you.
Watch your tongue!
Or we will take it from you.
No!
My gods!
Help me!
Have mercy on me!
Here I am, monster!
I’ll slaughter you and your family,
and the whole of Ithaca!
No! No!
Here I am! Here I am!
I’m the one you want!
Take me! Take me!
Father!
Father!
Odysseus?
Odysseus!
No!
What did he say to you, son?
Tell me! Tell me quickly!
What were his final words to you?
I don’t understand!
Telemachus...
What were his final words?
He said, third gift.
Third gift?
And then...
And then nothing more.
So clever.
The king of Ithaca.
Clever to his last.
Oh, goddess Athena.
My love.
You have suffered enough these past many days.
But the game’s over.
Odysseus...
Wins.
What do you mean?
He didn’t win.
He’s dead. He’s gone!
Do not be troubled, son of Odysseus.
Once again, your father’s glory honors me.
With his final breath,
your husband requested his last wish.
May I grant it?
Yes.
Yes, please.
Clever is indeed greater than good.
- Father! - He’s alive!
Goddess Athena, thank you.
It was your husband who outsmarted death.
I am glad to see you all reunited.
My son...
Oh, my son.
I was gone.
The goddess.
Athena has granted me my third wish.
My father more clever than the gods themselves.
The river Styx can wait...
But a moment longer.
Oh...
You took your time, old man.
The wind.
The wind was against me.
I have heard such stories.
You seem as if from a dream.
Are you really here?
Or are the gods still playing games.
I have not the strength for their sport any longer.
Nor do I.
Nor do I, my queen.
King of Ithaca, why have you returned to this place?
I have but one goal.
One destination.
Not Ithaca, not this house,
not the crown was my goal.
I care not for the seas or the skies.
I sought no monsters, nor gods.
I only sought you.
Only you.
You... You were the safe harbor I fought
so desperately to get home to.
And home you will stay.
Yes, I will.
Home.
The only journey worth the fight.
Home.
Home at last.

material.title: 蒂姆·库克 · 2019 斯坦福毕业演讲
material.subtitle: 英文原声 · 双语字幕 · 完整演讲

cues.en: Stanford University.
cues.zh: 斯坦福大学。

cues.en: Please join me in welcoming Tim Cook.
cues.zh: 请和我一起欢迎蒂姆·库克。

cues.en: Thank you. Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。谢谢。

cues.en: Good morning, Class of 2019!
cues.zh: 早上好，2019届毕业生！

cues.en: Thank you, President Tessier-Lavigne, for that very generous introduction.
cues.zh: 谢谢特西耶-拉维涅校长，感谢您如此慷慨的介绍。

cues.en: I'll do my best to earn it.
cues.zh: 我会尽力不辜负。

cues.en: Before I begin, I want to recognize everyone whose hard work made this celebration possible.
cues.zh: 在我开始之前，我想感谢所有为这次庆祝活动付出辛勤努力的人们。

cues.en: Including the groundskeepers, ushers, volunteers, and crew. Thank you.
cues.zh: 包括场地管理员、引导员、志愿者和工作人员。谢谢你们。

cues.en: I am deeply honored and frankly, a little astonished, to be invited to join you for this most meaningful of occasions.
cues.zh: 我深感荣幸，坦率地说，还有点惊讶，能应邀参加这意义非凡的盛会。

cues.en: Graduates, this is your day.
cues.zh: 毕业生们，这是你们的日子。

cues.en: But you didn't get here alone. Family and friends, teachers, mentors, loved ones, and of course, your parents.
cues.zh: 但你们并非独自来到这里。家人和朋友、老师、导师、亲人，当然还有你们的父母。

cues.en: All worked together to make you possible, and they share your joy today.
cues.zh: 都共同努力让你们成为可能，他们今天也分享你们的喜悦。

cues.en: Here on Father's Day, let's give the dads in particular a round of applause.
cues.zh: 今天父亲节，让我们特别为爸爸们鼓掌。

cues.en: Stanford is near to my heart, not least because I live just a mile and a half from here.
cues.zh: 斯坦福离我很近，不仅仅是因为我住在这里一英里半的地方。

cues.en: Of course, if my accent hasn't given it away, for the first part of my life, I had to admire this place from a distance.
cues.zh: 当然，如果我的口音还没有暴露，在我生命的前半段，我不得不远远地仰慕这个地方。

cues.en: I went to school on the other side of the country at Auburn University, in the heart of landlocked Eastern Alabama.
cues.zh: 我在国家的另一边，在奥本大学上学，位于内陆东阿拉巴马州的心脏地带。

cues.en: You may not know this.
cues.zh: 你们可能不知道。

cues.en: But I was on the sailing team all four years.
cues.zh: 但我参加了四年的帆船队。

cues.en: It wasn't easy.
cues.zh: 这并不容易。

cues.en: Back then, the closest marina was a three-hour drive. For practice, most of the time, we had to wait for a heavy rainstorm to flood the football field.
cues.zh: 那时，最近的码头有三个小时的车程。为了练习，大多数时候，我们不得不等待一场大暴雨淹没足球场。

cues.en: And tying knots is hard. Who knew?
cues.zh: 而且打绳结很难。谁知道呢？

cues.en: Yet somehow, against all odds, we managed to beat Stanford every time.
cues.zh: 但不知何故，尽管困难重重，我们每次都设法击败了斯坦福。

cues.en: We must have gotten lucky with the wind.
cues.zh: 我们一定是风向好才赢的。

cues.en: Kidding aside, I know the real reason I'm here, and I don't take it lightly.
cues.zh: 开个玩笑，我知道我来这里的真正原因，我不会掉以轻心。

cues.en: Stanford and Silicon Valley's roots are woven together. We're part of the same ecosystem.
cues.zh: 斯坦福和硅谷的根紧密相连。我们是同一个生态系统的一部分。

cues.en: It was true when Steve stood on the stage 14 years ago. It's true today, and presumably, it'll be true for a while longer still.
cues.zh: 14年前史蒂夫站在台上时就是如此。今天依然如此，而且可以想见，在未来一段时间内仍将如此。

cues.en: The past few decades have lifted us together.
cues.zh: 过去的几十年我们携手共进。

cues.en: But today, we gather at a moment that demands some reflection.
cues.zh: 但今天，我们聚集在这样一个需要反思的时刻。

cues.en: Fueled by caffeine and code, optimism and idealism, conviction and creativity.
cues.zh: 以咖啡因和代码为动力，以乐观和理想主义为驱动，以信念和创造力为支撑。

cues.en: Generations of Stanford graduates and dropouts have used technology to remake our society.
cues.zh: 一代又一代的斯坦福毕业生和辍学生利用技术重塑了我们的社会。

cues.en: But I think you would agree that lately, the results haven't been neat or straightforward.
cues.zh: 但我认为你们会同意，最近，结果并不那么整洁或直接。

cues.en: In just the four years that you've been here at the farm, things feel like they've taken a sharp turn.
cues.zh: 仅仅在你们在这里度过的四年里，事情似乎发生了急转弯。

cues.en: Crisis has tempered optimism. Consequences have challenged idealism, and reality has shaken blind faith.
cues.zh: 危机已经磨砺了乐观，后果已经挑战了理想主义，现实已经动摇了盲目信仰。

cues.en: And yet, we are still drawn here, for good reason.
cues.zh: 然而，我们仍然被吸引到这里，是有充分理由的。

cues.en: Big dreams live here.
cues.zh: 伟大的梦想在此孕育。

cues.en: As do the genius and passion to make them real.
cues.zh: 以及实现它们的才华与激情。

cues.en: In an age of cynicism, this place still believes
cues.zh: 在这个玩世不恭的时代，这里依然相信

cues.en: that the human capacity to solve problems is boundless.
cues.zh: 人类解决问题的能力是无限的。

cues.en: But so it seems is our potential to create them.
cues.zh: 但似乎我们制造问题的潜力也同样无限。

cues.en: That's what I'm interested in talking about today.
cues.zh: 这正是我今天想谈论的。

cues.en: Because if I've learned one thing, it's that technology
cues.zh: 因为如果我学到了一件事，那就是科技

cues.en: doesn't change who we are, it magnifies who we are.
cues.zh: 并不会改变我们是谁，而是放大我们是谁。

cues.en: The good and the bad.
cues.zh: 好的和坏的。

cues.en: Our problems in technology, in politics, wherever,
cues.zh: 我们在科技、政治，无论何处遇到的问题，

cues.en: are human problems.
cues.zh: 都是人类的问题。

cues.en: From the Garden of Eden to today, it's our humanity
cues.zh: 从伊甸园到今天，是我们的本性

cues.en: that got us into this mess.
cues.zh: 让我们陷入了困境。

cues.en: And it's our humanity that's going to have to get us out.
cues.zh: 也需要我们的本性来拯救我们。

cues.en: First things first.
cues.zh: 首先，我们得明白。

cues.en: Here's the plain fact: Silicon Valley is responsible for
cues.zh: 一个简单的事实是：硅谷是导致

cues.en: some of the most revolutionary inventions in modern history.
cues.zh: 现代史上许多革命性发明的责任方。

cues.en: From the first oscillator built in the Hewlett-Packard garage to the iPhones
cues.zh: 从惠普车库里制造的第一个振荡器，到我敢说你们手中持有的iPhone，

cues.en: that I know you're holding in your hands.
cues.zh: 再到你们手中的iPhone。

cues.en: Social media, shareable videos, snaps and stories that connect half the people on Earth.
cues.zh: 社交媒体、可分享的视频、Snapchat和Stories，连接了地球上近半数的人。

cues.en: They all trace their roots to Stanford's backyard.
cues.zh: 它们都可追溯到斯坦福的后院。

cues.en: But lately, it seems this industry is becoming better known for a less noble innovation.
cues.zh: 但最近，这个行业似乎因一项不太光彩的创新而闻名。

cues.en: The belief that you can claim credit without accepting responsibility.
cues.zh: 那就是可以邀功而不承担责任的观念。

cues.en: We see it every day now.
cues.zh: 我们现在每天都能看到。

cues.en: With every data breach, every privacy violation,
cues.zh: 每一次数据泄露，每一次隐私侵犯，

cues.en: every blind eye turned to hate speech.
cues.zh: 每一次对仇恨言论视而不见。

cues.en: Fake news poisoning our national conversation.
cues.zh: 假新闻毒害着我们的国家对话。

cues.en: The false miracles in exchange for a single drop of your blood.
cues.zh: 虚假的奇迹，却要你一滴血的代价。

cues.en: Too many seem to think that good intentions excuse away harmful outcomes.
cues.zh: 太多人似乎认为，好意可以为有害的后果开脱。

cues.en: But whether you like it or not, what you build and what you create define who you are.
cues.zh: 但无论你是否喜欢，你所建造和创造的东西定义了你是谁。

cues.en: It feels a bit crazy that anyone should have to say this.
cues.zh: 感觉有点疯狂，竟然有人需要说出这句话。

cues.en: But if you've built a chaos factory, you can't dodge responsibility for the chaos.
cues.zh: 但如果你建造了一个混乱工厂，你就不能逃避混乱的责任。

cues.en: Taking responsibility means having the courage to think things through.
cues.zh: 承担责任意味着要有勇气深思熟虑。

cues.en: And there are few areas where this is more important than privacy.
cues.zh: 而在隐私方面，这一点尤其重要。

cues.en: If we accept as normal and unavoidable that everything in our lives can be aggregated,
cues.zh: 如果我们接受，我们生活中的一切都可以被聚合、

cues.en: sold, or even leaked in the event of a hack,
cues.zh: 出售，甚至在被黑客攻击时泄露，这都是正常且不可避免的，

cues.en: then we lose so much more than data.
cues.zh: 那么我们失去的将远不止数据。

cues.en: We lose the freedom to be human.
cues.zh: 我们失去了作为人的自由。

cues.en: Think about what's at stake.
cues.zh: 想想我们面临的风险。

cues.en: Everything you write, everything you say,
cues.zh: 你写下的每一句话，你说的每一句话，

cues.en: every topic of curiosity, every stray thought,
cues.zh: 每一个好奇的话题，每一个随意的想法，

cues.en: every impulsive purchase, every moment of frustration or weakness.
cues.zh: 每一次冲动的购买，每一次沮丧或软弱的时刻。

cues.en: Every gripe or complaint, every secret shared in confidence.
cues.zh: 每一次抱怨或不满，每一次秘密的分享。

cues.en: In a world without digital privacy, even if you have done nothing wrong other than think differently,
cues.zh: 在一个没有数字隐私的世界里，即使你没有做错任何事，只是想法不同，

cues.en: you begin to censor yourself.
cues.zh: 你就会开始自我审查。

cues.en: Not entirely at first.
cues.zh: 一开始不是完全的。

cues.en: Just a little bit.
cues.zh: 只是稍微一点。

cues.en: Just a little.
cues.zh: 只是一点点。

cues.en: Bit by bit.
cues.zh: 一点一滴地。

cues.en: To risk less, to hope less.
cues.zh: 为了承担更少的风险，抱有更少的希望。

cues.en: To imagine less.
cues.zh: 为了想象得更少。

cues.en: To dare less.
cues.zh: 为了胆量更小。

cues.en: To create less.
cues.zh: 为了创造得更少。

cues.en: To try less.
cues.zh: 为了尝试得更少。

cues.en: To talk less.
cues.zh: 为了说得更少。

cues.en: To think less.
cues.zh: 为了思考得更少。

cues.en: The chilling effect of digital surveillance is profound.
cues.zh: 数字监控的寒蝉效应是深远的。

cues.en: And it touches everything.
cues.zh: 它触及一切。

cues.en: What a small, unimaginative world we would end up with.
cues.zh: 我们最终会生活在一个多么渺小、缺乏想象力的世界里。

cues.en: Not entirely at first.
cues.zh: 一开始并非完全如此。

cues.en: Just a little.
cues.zh: 只是一点点。

cues.en: Bit by bit.
cues.zh: 一点一滴地。

cues.en: Ironically, it's the kind of environment that would have stopped Silicon Valley before it had ever gotten started.
cues.zh: 讽刺的是，这种环境本可以在硅谷起步之前就扼杀它。

cues.en: If we believe that freedom means an environment where great ideas can take root.
cues.zh: 如果我们相信自由意味着一个伟大的想法能够生根发芽的环境。

cues.en: Where they can grow and be nurtured without fear of irrational restrictions or burdens.
cues.zh: 在那里它们可以成长和被培育，而不必担心不合理的限制或负担。

cues.en: Then it's our duty to change course.
cues.zh: 那么我们就有责任改变方向。

cues.en: Because your generation ought to have the same freedom to shape the future as the generation that came before.
cues.zh: 因为你们这一代应该拥有与前一代人同等的塑造未来的自由。

cues.en: Graduates, at the very least, learn from these mistakes.
cues.zh: 毕业生们，至少要从这些错误中吸取教训。

cues.en: If you want to take credit, first learn to take responsibility.
cues.zh: 如果你想获得赞誉，首先要学会承担责任。

cues.en: Now, a lot of you, the vast majority, won't find yourselves in tech at all.
cues.zh: 现在，你们中的许多人，绝大多数人，根本不会进入科技行业。

cues.en: That's as it should be.
cues.zh: 这才是应有的样子。

cues.en: We need your minds at work far and wide.
cues.zh: 我们需要你们的智慧在各行各业发挥作用。

cues.en: Because our challenges are great, and they can't be solved by any single industry.
cues.zh: 因为我们的挑战是巨大的，任何一个行业都无法解决。

cues.en: No matter where you go, no matter what you do, I know you will be ambitious.
cues.zh: 无论你们去哪里，无论你们做什么，我知道你们都会雄心勃勃。

cues.en: You wouldn't be here today if you weren't.
cues.zh: 如果不是这样，你们今天就不会在这里。

cues.en: Match that ambition with humility.
cues.zh: 将这种雄心与谦逊相结合。

cues.en: A humility of purpose.
cues.zh: 一种有目的的谦逊。

cues.en: That doesn't mean being tamer, being smaller, being less in what you do.
cues.zh: 这并不意味着要变得更驯服、更渺小、在你们所做的事情上有所减少。

cues.en: It's the opposite.
cues.zh: 恰恰相反。

cues.en: It's about serving something greater.
cues.zh: 它是关于服务更伟大的事物。

cues.en: The author Madeleine L'Engle wrote, "Humility is throwing oneself away."
cues.zh: 作家马德琳·英格写道：“谦逊是抛弃自我。”

cues.en: In complete concentration on something or someone else.
cues.zh: 完全专注于某事或某人。

cues.en: In other words, whatever you do with your life, be a builder.
cues.zh: 换句话说，无论你用你的生命做什么，都要成为一个建设者。

cues.en: You don't have to start from scratch to build something monumental.
cues.zh: 你不必从零开始才能建造出不朽的东西。

cues.en: And conversely, the best founders, the ones whose creations last, and whose reputations grow rather than shrink with passing time.
cues.zh: 反之，最优秀的创始人，那些创造能够持久、声誉随着时间推移而增长而非缩减的人。

cues.en: They spend most of their time building, piece by piece.
cues.zh: 他们花费大部分时间，一点一滴地进行建设。

cues.en: Builders are comfortable in the belief that their life's work will one day be bigger than them, bigger than any one person.
cues.zh: 建设者们安于相信他们毕生的工作有一天会比他们自己更伟大，比任何一个人都更伟大。

cues.en: They're mindful that its effects will span generations.
cues.zh: 他们意识到其影响将跨越几代人。

cues.en: That's not an accident.
cues.zh: 这不是偶然的。

cues.en: In a way, it's the whole point.
cues.zh: 在某种程度上，这就是全部意义所在。

cues.en: In a few days, we will mark the 50th anniversary of the riots at Stonewall.
cues.zh: 几天后，我们将迎来斯通沃尔骚乱50周年。

cues.en: When the patrons of the Stonewall Inn showed up that night, people of all races, gay and transgender, young and old.
cues.zh: 当斯通沃尔旅馆的顾客们在那晚出现时，各种肤色的人，同性恋和跨性别者，年轻和年老的人。

cues.en: When the door was busted open by police, it was not the knock of opportunity or the call of destiny.
cues.zh: 当警察破门而入时，那不是机遇的敲门声，也不是命运的召唤。

cues.en: It was just another instance of the world telling them that they ought to feel worthless for being different.
cues.zh: 这只是世界又一次告诉他们，他们因为与众不同而应该感到渺小。

cues.en: But the group gathered there felt something strengthened in them, a conviction that they deserved something better than the shadows.
cues.zh: 但聚集在那里的团体感觉到他们内心有什么东西得到了加强，一种信念，他们值得比阴影更好的东西。

cues.en: and better than oblivion.
cues.zh: 也比遗忘更好。

cues.en: And if it wasn't going to be given, then they were going to have to build it themselves.
cues.zh: 如果它不会被给予，那么他们就必须自己去建造它。

cues.en: I was eight years old and a thousand miles away when Stonewall happened.
cues.zh: 斯通沃尔事件发生时，我八岁，远在千里之外。

cues.en: There were no news alerts, no way for photos to go viral, no mechanism for a kid on the Gulf Coast to hear these unlikely heroes tell their stories.
cues.zh: 没有新闻警报，没有照片可以病毒式传播，也没有机制让海湾沿岸的孩子听到这些不太可能的英雄讲述他们的故事。

cues.en: Greenwich Village may as well have been a different planet.
cues.zh: 格林威治村可能就像是另一个星球。

cues.en: Though I can tell you that the slurs and hatreds were the same.
cues.zh: 尽管我可以告诉你，那些诽谤和仇恨是一样的。

cues.en: What I would not know for a long time was what I owed to a group of people I never knew in a place I'd never been.
cues.zh: 我长期以来都不知道，我欠一群我从未认识的人，在一个我从未去过的地方。

cues.en: Yet I will never stop being grateful for what they had the courage to build.
cues.zh: 但我永远不会停止感激他们有勇气去建造的东西。

cues.en: Graduates, being a builder is about believing that you cannot possibly be the greatest cause on this earth.
cues.zh: 毕业生们，成为一个建设者就是相信你不可能成为这个地球上最伟大的事业。

cues.en: because you aren't built to last.
cues.zh: 因为你不是为了长久而存在的。

cues.en: It's about making peace with the fact that you won't be here for the end of the story.
cues.zh: 这是关于接受你将无法见证故事的结局这一事实。

cues.en: That brings me to my last bit of advice.
cues.zh: 这让我想到我的最后一条建议。

cues.en: 14 years ago, Steve stood on this stage and told your predecessors, your time is limited.
cues.zh: 14年前，史蒂夫站在这舞台上告诉你的前任们，你们的时间有限。

cues.en: So don't waste it living someone else's life.
cues.zh: 所以不要浪费它去过别人的生活。

cues.en: Here's my corollary.
cues.zh: 这是我的推论。

cues.en: Your mentors may leave you prepared, but they can't leave you ready.
cues.zh: 你的导师可能会让你做好准备，但他们无法让你万事俱备。

cues.en: When Steve got sick, I had hardwired my thinking to the belief that he would get better.
cues.zh: 当史蒂夫生病时，我一直坚信他会好起来的。

cues.en: I not only thought he would hold on, I was convinced down to my core that he'd still be guiding Apple long after I myself was gone.
cues.zh: 我不仅认为他会坚持下去，我内心深处坚信，即使我不在了，他也会继续领导苹果。

cues.en: Then one day, he called me over to his house and told me that it wasn't going to be that way.
cues.zh: 然后有一天，他叫我去他家，告诉我事情不会那样发展。

cues.en: Even then, I was convinced he would stay on as chairman, that he would step back from the day-to-day but always be there as a sounding board.
cues.zh: 即使那时，我也坚信他会继续担任董事长，他会从日常事务中退居幕后，但会一直作为我的咨询对象。

cues.en: But there was no reason to believe that.
cues.zh: 但没有理由相信这一点。

cues.en: I never should have thought it.
cues.zh: 我本不该那样想。

cues.en: The facts were all there.
cues.zh: 事实摆在那里。

cues.en: And when he was gone, truly gone, I learned the real visceral difference between preparation and readiness.
cues.zh: 当他离开，真正离开时，我才明白了准备和就绪之间真正的、切身的区别。

cues.en: It was the loneliest I've ever felt in my life, by an order of magnitude.
cues.zh: 那是我一生中最孤独的时刻，程度之深难以想象。

cues.en: It was one of those moments where you can be surrounded by people, yet you don't really see, hear, or feel them.
cues.zh: 那是那种你被人群包围，却无法真正看见、听见或感受到他们的时刻。

cues.en: But I could sense their expectations.
cues.zh: 但我能感觉到他们的期望。

cues.en: When the dust settled, all I knew was that I was going to have to be the best version
cues.zh: 当尘埃落定，我只知道我必须成为最好的版本

cues.en: I knew that if you got out of bed every morning and set your watch by what other people expect or demand, it'd drive you crazy.
cues.zh: 我知道，如果你每天早上起床，就按照别人的期望或要求来安排自己的生活，那会让你发疯。

cues.en: So what was true then is true now.
cues.zh: 所以，当时是真的，现在也是真的。

cues.en: Don't waste your time living someone else's life.
cues.zh: 不要浪费时间去过别人的生活。

cues.en: Don't try to emulate the people who came before you to the exclusion of everything else, contorting into a shape that doesn't fit.
cues.zh: 不要试图模仿你之前的人，而排斥其他一切，扭曲成不适合你的形状。

cues.en: It takes too much mental effort.
cues.zh: 这需要太多的精神努力。

cues.en: Effort that should be dedicated to creating and building.
cues.zh: 本应致力于创造和建设的努力。

cues.en: You'll waste precious time trying to rewire your every thought.
cues.zh: 你将浪费宝贵的时间来试图重塑你的每一个想法。

cues.en: And in the meantime, you won't be fooling anybody.
cues.zh: 同时，你也不会欺骗任何人。

cues.en: Graduates, the fact is, when your time comes,
cues.zh: 毕业生们，事实是，当你们的时机到来时，

cues.en: and it will,
cues.zh: 它一定会到来，

cues.en: you'll never be ready.
cues.zh: 你们永远不会准备好。

cues.en: But you're not supposed to be.
cues.zh: 但你们本来就不该准备好。

cues.en: Find the hope in the unexpected.
cues.zh: 在意外中寻找希望。

cues.en: Find the courage in the challenge.
cues.zh: 在挑战中寻找勇气。

cues.en: Find your vision on the solitary road.
cues.zh: 在孤独的道路上找到你的愿景。

cues.en: Don't get distracted.
cues.zh: 不要分心。

cues.en: There are too many people who won't credit without responsibility.
cues.zh: 有太多的人，在没有责任的情况下却想要获得认可。

cues.en: Too many who show up for the ribbon cutting without building anything worth a damn.
cues.zh: 太多的人，在什么有价值的东西都没建成就来参加剪彩。

cues.en: Be different.
cues.zh: 与众不同。

cues.en: Leave something worthy.
cues.zh: 留下一些有价值的东西。

cues.en: And always remember
cues.zh: 并且永远记住

cues.en: that you can't take it with you.
cues.zh: 你无法带走它。

cues.en: You're going to have to pass it on.
cues.zh: 你必须把它传承下去。

cues.en: Thank you very much
cues.zh: 非常感谢

cues.en: and congratulations to the class of 2019!
cues.zh: 祝贺2019届毕业生！

material.title: 特朗普 · 2017 就职演讲
material.subtitle: 英文原声 · 双语字幕 · 完整演讲

cues.en: Ladies and gentlemen, it's an honor to introduce the Chief Justice of the United States, John G. Roberts Jr., who will administer the presidential oath of office. Everyone, please stand.
cues.zh: 女士们，先生们，我很荣幸介绍美国首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨，他将主持总统就职宣誓。请大家起立。

cues.en: Please raise your right hand and repeat after me.
cues.zh: 请举起右手，跟我重复。

cues.en: I, Donald John Trump, do solemnly swear.
cues.zh: 我，唐纳德·约翰·特朗普，郑重宣誓。

cues.en: That I will faithfully execute.
cues.zh: 我将忠实地执行。

cues.en: The office of President of the United States.
cues.zh: 美利坚合众国总统的职务。

cues.en: And will to the best of my ability.
cues.zh: 并尽我所能。

cues.en: Preserve, protect and defend.
cues.zh: 维护、保护和捍卫。

cues.en: The Constitution of the United States.
cues.zh: 美利坚合众国宪法。

cues.en: So help me God.
cues.zh: 愿上帝保佑我。

cues.en: Congratulations, Mr. President.
cues.zh: 恭喜您，总统先生。

cues.en: What a great honor to be able to introduce for the first time ever anywhere the 45th President of the United States of America, Donald J. Trump.
cues.zh: 能首次向大家介绍美国第45任总统唐纳德·J·特朗普，这是莫大的荣幸。

cues.en: Chief Justice Roberts, President Carter, President Clinton, President Bush, President Obama, fellow Americans, and people of the world, thank you.
cues.zh: 首席大法官罗伯茨，卡特总统，克林顿总统，布什总统，奥巴马总统，美国同胞们，以及全世界人民，谢谢你们。

cues.en: We, the citizens of America, are now joined in a great national effort to rebuild our country and restore its promise for all of our people.
cues.zh: 我们，美国公民，现在正共同努力，进行一项伟大的国家事业，重建我们的国家，并为我们所有人民恢复其承诺。

cues.en: Together, we will determine the course of America and the world for many, many years to come.
cues.zh: 我们将共同决定美国和世界的未来走向，在未来许多许多年里。

cues.en: We will face challenges. We will confront hardships, but we will get the job done.
cues.zh: 我们将面临挑战，我们将面对困难，但我们将完成任务。

cues.en: Every four years, we gather on these steps to carry out the orderly and peaceful transfer of power. And we are grateful to President Obama.
cues.zh: 每四年，我们都会聚集在这些台阶上，进行有序和平的权力交接。我们感谢奥巴马总统。

cues.en: and we are grateful to President Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama for their gracious aid throughout this transition.
cues.zh: 我们感谢奥巴马总统和第一夫人米歇尔·奥巴马在这次过渡期间给予的慷慨帮助。

cues.en: They have been magnificent.
cues.zh: 他们表现得非常出色。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。

cues.en: Today's ceremony, however, has very special meaning.
cues.zh: 然而，今天的仪式具有非常特殊的意义。

cues.en: Because today, we are not merely transferring power from one administration to another, or from one party to another.
cues.zh: 因为今天，我们不仅仅是从一个政府转移权力到另一个政府，或者从一个政党转移到另一个政党。

cues.en: But we are transferring power from Washington D.C. and giving it back to you, the people.
cues.zh: 而是我们将权力从华盛顿特区转移出去，并将它还给你们，人民。

cues.en: For too long, a small group in our nation's capital has reaped the rewards of government while the people have borne the cost.
cues.zh: 长期以来，我们国家首都的一小群人从中获益，而人民却承担了代价。

cues.en: Washington flourished, but the people did not share in its wealth.
cues.zh: 华盛顿繁荣了，但人民并未分享其财富。

cues.en: Politicians prospered, but the jobs left, and the factories closed.
cues.zh: 政客们发财了，但工作岗位却流失了，工厂也关闭了。

cues.en: The establishment protected itself, but not the citizens of our country.
cues.zh: 建制派保护了自己，却没有保护我们国家的公民。

cues.en: Their victories have not been your victories. Their triumphs have not been your triumphs.
cues.zh: 他们的胜利不是你们的胜利。他们的辉煌不是你们的辉煌。

cues.en: And while they celebrated in our nation's capital, there was little to celebrate for struggling families all across our land.
cues.zh: 当他们在我们国家首都庆祝时，我们国土上挣扎的家庭却没有什么可庆祝的。

cues.en: That all changes, starting right here and right now.
cues.zh: 这一切都将改变，从现在开始，从这里开始。

cues.en: Because this moment is your moment. It belongs to you.
cues.zh: 因为这一刻是你们的时刻。它属于你们。

cues.en: It belongs to everyone gathered here today, and everyone watching all across America.
cues.zh: 它属于今天聚集在这里的每一个人，以及全美国正在观看的每一个人。

cues.en: This is your day. This is your celebration.
cues.zh: 这是你们的日子。这是你们的庆祝。

cues.en: And this, the United States of America, is your country.
cues.zh: 而这，美利坚合众国，是你们的国家。

cues.en: What truly matters is not which party controls our government, but whether our government is controlled by the people.
cues.zh: 真正重要的是哪个政党控制我们的政府，而是我们的政府是否由人民控制。

cues.en: January 20th, 2017, will be remembered as the day the people became the rulers of this nation again.
cues.zh: 2017年1月20日将被铭记为人民再次成为这个国家统治者的日子。

cues.en: The forgotten men and women of our country will be forgotten no longer.
cues.zh: 我们国家被遗忘的男女将不再被遗忘。

cues.en: Everyone is listening to you now.
cues.zh: 现在每个人都在听你们说话。

cues.en: You came by the tens of millions to become part of a historic movement, the likes of which the world has never seen before.
cues.zh: 你们数千万人加入了一个史无前例的历史性运动。

cues.en: At the center of this movement is a crucial conviction: that a nation exists to serve its citizens.
cues.zh: 这个运动的核心是一个关键的信念：一个国家存在的目的是服务于它的公民。

cues.en: Americans want great schools for their children, safe neighborhoods for their families, and good jobs for themselves.
cues.zh: 美国人希望他们的孩子有好的学校，他们的家庭有安全的社区，他们自己有好的工作。

cues.en: These are just and reasonable demands of righteous people and a righteous public.
cues.zh: 这些是正直的人民和正直的公众公正而合理的要求。

cues.en: But for too many of our citizens, a different reality exists.
cues.zh: 但对我们太多的公民来说，现实却截然不同。

cues.en: Mothers and children trapped in poverty in our inner cities.
cues.zh: 母亲和孩子被困在我们市中心的贫困之中。

cues.en: Rusted out factories scattered like tombstones across the landscape of our nation.
cues.zh: 锈迹斑斑的工厂像墓碑一样散落在我们国家的土地上。

cues.en: And education system, flush with cash, but which leaves our young and beautiful students deprived of all knowledge.
cues.zh: 以及一个资金充裕的教育系统，却让我们的年轻美丽的学子们一无所知。

cues.en: And the crime, and the gangs, and the drugs that have stolen too many lives and robbed our country of so much unrealized potential.
cues.zh: 还有那些偷走了太多生命、剥夺了我国无数未实现潜力的犯罪、帮派和毒品。

cues.en: This American carnage stops right here and stops right now.
cues.zh: 这种美国的惨状到此为止，立即停止。

cues.en: We are one nation, and their pain is our pain.
cues.zh: 我们是一个国家，他们的痛苦就是我们的痛苦。

cues.en: Their dreams are our dreams, and their success will be our success.
cues.zh: 他们的梦想就是我们的梦想，他们的成功就是我们的成功。

cues.en: We share one heart, one home, and one glorious destiny.
cues.zh: 我们共享一颗心，一个家园，和一个光荣的命运。

cues.en: The oath of office I take today is an oath of allegiance to all Americans.
cues.zh: 我今天宣誓就职，是对所有美国人的效忠誓言。

cues.en: For many decades, we've enriched foreign industry at the expense of American industry.
cues.zh: 几十年来，我们以牺牲美国工业为代价来丰富外国工业。

cues.en: Subsidized the armies of other countries while allowing for the very sad depletion of our military.
cues.zh: 资助其他国家的军队，同时却允许我们的军队遭受非常可悲的消耗。

cues.en: We've defended other nations' borders while refusing to defend our own.
cues.zh: 我们保卫了其他国家的边界，却拒绝保卫我们自己的边界。

cues.en: And spent trillions and trillions of dollars overseas, while America's infrastructure has fallen into disrepair and decay.
cues.zh: 并在海外花费了数万亿美元，而美国的基础设施却已破败不堪。

cues.en: We've made other countries rich, while the wealth, strength, and confidence of our country has dissipated over the horizon.
cues.zh: 我们使其他国家变得富有，而我们国家的财富、力量和信心却已消失在天际。

cues.en: One by one, the factories shuttered and left our shores.
cues.zh: 一家一家工厂倒闭，离开了我们的海岸。

cues.en: With not even a thought about the millions and millions of American workers that were left behind.
cues.zh: 甚至没有想过那些被抛在身后的数百万美国工人。

cues.en: The wealth of our middle class has been ripped from their homes and then redistributed all across the world.
cues.zh: 我们中产阶级的财富被从他们的家中掠夺，然后重新分配到世界各地。

cues.en: But that is the past.
cues.zh: 但那已是过去。

cues.en: And now, we are looking only to the future.
cues.zh: 现在，我们只着眼于未来。

cues.en: We assembled here today are issuing a new decree to be heard in every city, in every foreign capital, and in every hall of power.
cues.zh: 我们今天在此集会，发布一项新法令，让每个城市、每个外国首都、每个权力殿堂都能听到。

cues.en: From this day forward, a new vision will govern our land.
cues.zh: 从今天起，一个新的愿景将统治我们的土地。

cues.en: From this day forward, it's going to be only America first. America first.
cues.zh: 从今天起，将只有美国优先。美国优先。

cues.en: Every decision on trade, on taxes, on immigration, on foreign affairs will be made to benefit American workers and American families.
cues.zh: 每一项关于贸易、税收、移民、外交事务的决定，都将是为了使美国工人和美国家庭受益。

cues.en: We must protect our borders from the ravages of other countries making our products, stealing our companies, and destroying our jobs.
cues.zh: 我们必须保护我们的边界，免受其他国家制造我们的产品、窃取我们的公司、摧毁我们工作的侵害。

cues.en: Protection will lead to great prosperity and strength.
cues.zh: 保护将带来巨大的繁荣和力量。

cues.en: I will fight for you with every breath in my body, and I will never, ever let you down.
cues.zh: 我将用我身体的每一口气为你而战，我永远，永远不会让你失望。

cues.en: America will start winning again, winning like never before.
cues.zh: 美国将重新开始获胜，以前所未有的方式获胜。

cues.en: We will bring back our jobs.
cues.zh: 我们将带回我们的工作。

cues.en: We will bring back our borders.
cues.zh: 我们将带回我们的边境。

cues.en: We will bring back our wealth.
cues.zh: 我们将带回我们的财富。

cues.en: And we will bring back our dreams.
cues.zh: 我们将带回我们的梦想。

cues.en: We will build new roads, and highways, and bridges, and airports, and tunnels, and railways all across our wonderful nation.
cues.zh: 我们将建造新的道路、高速公路、桥梁、机场、隧道和铁路，遍布我们伟大的国家。

cues.en: We will get our people off of welfare and back to work, rebuilding our country with American hands and American labor.
cues.zh: 我们将让人们摆脱福利，重返工作岗位，用美国人的双手和美国劳动力重建我们的国家。

cues.en: We will follow two simple rules: Buy American and hire American.
cues.zh: 我们将遵循两条简单的规则：购买美国货，雇佣美国人。

cues.en: We will seek friendship and goodwill with the nations of the world, but we do so with the understanding that it is the right of all nations to put their own interests first.
cues.zh: 我们将寻求与世界各国建立友谊和善意，但我们这样做是基于所有国家都应将自身利益放在首位的理解。

cues.en: We do not seek to impose our way of life on anyone, but rather to let it shine as an example. We will shine for everyone to follow.
cues.zh: 我们不寻求将我们的生活方式强加给任何人，而是让它闪耀成为榜样。我们将闪耀，供所有人效仿。

cues.en: We will reinforce all alliances and form new ones, and unite the civilized world against radical Islamic terrorism, which we will eradicate completely from the face of the earth.
cues.zh: 我们将加强所有联盟并形成新的联盟，团结文明世界对抗激进的伊斯兰恐怖主义，我们将彻底根除它，使其从地球上消失。

cues.en: At the bedrock of our politics will be a total allegiance to the United States of America.
cues.zh: 我们政治的基石将是对美利坚合众国的完全效忠。

cues.en: And through our loyalty to our country, we will rediscover our loyalty to each other.
cues.zh: 通过我们对国家的忠诚，我们将重新发现我们彼此之间的忠诚。

cues.en: When you open your heart to patriotism, there is no room for prejudice.
cues.zh: 当你向爱国主义敞开心扉时，就没有偏见的容身之地。

cues.en: The Bible tells us how good and pleasant it is when God's people live together in unity.
cues.zh: 圣经告诉我们，当上帝的子民团结一致地生活在一起时，是多么美好和令人愉悦。

cues.en: We must speak our minds openly, debate our disagreements honestly, but always pursue solidarity.
cues.zh: 我们必须坦率地表达自己的想法，诚实地辩论我们的分歧，但要始终追求团结。

cues.en: When America is united, America is totally unstoppable.
cues.zh: 当美国团结起来时，美国是完全不可阻挡的。

cues.en: There should be no fear.
cues.zh: 不应有恐惧。

cues.en: We are protected, and we will always be protected.
cues.zh: 我们受到保护，我们将永远受到保护。

cues.en: We will be protected by the great men and women of our military and law enforcement.
cues.zh: 我们将受到我们军队和执法部门的伟大男女的保护。

cues.en: And most importantly, we will be protected by God.
cues.zh: 最重要的是，我们将受到上帝的保护。

cues.en: Finally, we must think big and dream even bigger.
cues.zh: 最后，我们必须想得大，梦想得更大。

cues.en: In America, we understand that a nation is only living as long as it is striving.
cues.zh: 在美国，我们明白一个国家只有在努力奋斗时才能生存。

cues.en: We will no longer accept politicians who are all talk and no action, constantly complaining but never doing anything about it.
cues.zh: 我们不再接受那些只会空谈、毫无行动、不断抱怨却从不采取任何措施的政客。

cues.en: The time for empty talk is over.
cues.zh: 空谈的时代已经结束了。

cues.en: Now arrives the hour of action.
cues.zh: 现在是行动的时刻了。

cues.en: Do not allow anyone to tell you that it cannot be done.
cues.zh: 不要让任何人告诉你，这件事做不到。

cues.en: No challenge can match the heart and fight and spirit of America.
cues.zh: 没有任何挑战能匹敌美国的决心、斗志和精神。

cues.en: We will not fail.
cues.zh: 我们不会失败。

cues.en: Our country will thrive and prosper again.
cues.zh: 我们的国家将再次繁荣昌盛。

cues.en: We stand at the birth of a new millennium, ready to unlock the mysteries of space.
cues.zh: 我们正站在新千年的开端，准备解开太空的奥秘。

cues.en: To free the Earth from the miseries of disease and to harness the energies, industries and technologies of tomorrow.
cues.zh: 将地球从疾病的痛苦中解脱出来，并利用未来的能源、产业和技术。

cues.en: A new national pride will stir ourselves, lift our sights and heal our divisions.
cues.zh: 新的民族自豪感将激励我们，提升我们的视野，弥合我们的分歧。

cues.en: It's time to remember that old wisdom our soldiers will never forget.
cues.zh: 是时候记住我们士兵们永远不会忘记的古老智慧了。

cues.en: That whether we are black or brown or white, we all bleed the same red blood of patriots.
cues.zh: 无论我们是黑人、棕色人还是白人，我们都流淌着同样的爱国者鲜血。

cues.en: We all enjoy the same glorious freedoms and we all salute the same great American flag.
cues.zh: 我们都享有同样的辉煌自由，我们都向同一面伟大的美国国旗致敬。

cues.en: And whether a child is born in the urban sprawl of Detroit or the windswept plains of Nebraska, they look up at the same night sky.
cues.zh: 无论一个孩子出生在底特律的城市蔓延地带，还是内布拉斯加州风吹过的平原，他们都仰望同一片夜空。

cues.en: They fill their heart with the same dreams and they are infused with the breath of life by the same Almighty Creator.
cues.zh: 他们心中充满同样的梦想，并被同一位全能的造物主赋予生命的气息。

cues.en: So to all Americans, in every city, near and far, small and large, from mountain to mountain, from ocean to ocean, hear these words:
cues.zh: 所以，所有美国人，无论在哪个城市，无论远近，无论大小，从山到山，从海到海，请听这些话：

cues.en: You will never be ignored again.
cues.zh: 你们再也不会被忽视了。

cues.en: Your voice, your hopes and your dreams will define our American destiny.
cues.zh: 你们的声音、你们的希望和你们的梦想将定义我们美国的命运。

cues.en: And your courage and goodness and love will forever guide us along the way.
cues.zh: 你们的勇气、善良和爱将永远指引我们前进的道路。

cues.en: Together, we will make America strong again.
cues.zh: 我们将共同让美国再次强大。

cues.en: We will make America wealthy again.
cues.zh: 我们将共同让美国再次富裕。

cues.en: We will make America proud again.
cues.zh: 我们将共同让美国再次自豪。

cues.en: We will make America safe again.
cues.zh: 我们将共同让美国再次安全。

cues.en: And yes, together, we will make America great again.
cues.zh: 是的，我们将共同让美国再次伟大。

cues.en: Thank you. God bless you, and God bless America.
cues.zh: 谢谢。上帝保佑你们，上帝保佑美国。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。

cues.en: God bless America.
cues.zh: 上帝保佑美国。

material.title: J.K. 罗琳 · 2008 哈佛毕业演讲
material.subtitle: 英文原声 · 双语字幕 · 完整演讲

cues.en: Last summer, in a grand celebration of literature, Harvard Square and Harvard Yard, historically known as the place for Hollowood Halls filled with books, was transformed into Hogwarts Square.
cues.zh: 去年夏天，在一场盛大的文学庆典中，哈佛广场和哈佛庭院，历史上被称为装满书籍的霍洛伍德大厅，被改造成了霍格沃茨广场。

cues.en: This summer festival celebrated the midnight release of Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, the seventh and final installment in the wildly popular series.
cues.zh: 这个夏日庆典庆祝了《哈利·波特与死亡圣器》的午夜发行，这是这个广受欢迎系列的第七部也是最后一部。

cues.en: Hordes of people, children and adults alike, dressed in elaborate wizard costumes, stood in line for hours at the Coop to purchase copies of the book.
cues.zh: 成群结队的人们，无论老少，都穿着精致的巫师服装，在Coop排队数小时购买这本书的副本。

cues.en: Dozens of restaurants and stores stayed open late and posted Harry Potter themed specials and a three-hour concert capped off the evening in a packed Tarrytown Theater.
cues.zh: 数十家餐馆和商店彻夜营业，并发布了哈利·波特主题的特价商品，一场三小时的音乐会结束了在挤满人的塔里敦剧院的夜晚。

cues.en: Today, Tarrytown Theater is once again packed with children and adults, and we are pleased to welcome one of the most successful authors of our time.
cues.zh: 今天，塔里敦剧院再次挤满了儿童和成人，我们很高兴欢迎我们这个时代最成功的作家之一。

cues.en: Her books have set sales records and have won many awards, probably because the Harry Potter stories provide a familiar backdrop for readers who can empathize with the young protagonist adrift in a sometimes cruel and challenging world.
cues.zh: 她的书创下了销售记录并赢得了许多奖项，这可能是因为哈利·波特的故事为那些能够同情年轻主角在有时残酷和充满挑战的世界中漂泊的读者提供了一个熟悉的环境。

cues.en: In addition to her vast contributions to literature, she is also noted for the social, moral, and political inspiration she has given her fans. A notable philanthropist, she has established the Volant Charitable Trust, which donates millions of dollars to aid women and children and to combat poverty and social inequality.
cues.zh: 除了她对文学的巨大贡献外，她还因其对粉丝的社会、道德和政治启示而闻名。她是一位杰出的慈善家，成立了Volant慈善信托基金，该基金捐赠数百万美元以援助妇女和儿童，并对抗贫困和社会不平等。

cues.en: The fund also gives to organizations that aid children, one-parent families, and multiple sclerosis research. She herself has noted that a person has a moral responsibility when you've been given far more than you need to do wise things with it and to give intelligently.
cues.zh: 该基金还捐赠给援助儿童、单亲家庭和多发性硬化症研究的组织。她本人曾指出，当一个人拥有的远超所需时，就有道德责任明智地利用它并有智慧地给予。

cues.en: And now I give you Ms. J.K. Rowling.
cues.zh: 现在我向大家介绍J.K.罗琳女士。

cues.en: President Faust, members of the Harvard Corporation and the Board of Overseers, members of the faculty, proud parents, and above all, graduates.
cues.zh: 福斯特校长，哈佛公司和监督委员会的成员，教职员工，骄傲的父母们，以及最重要的是，毕业生们。

cues.en: The first thing I would like to say is thank you.
cues.zh: 我想说的第一件事是谢谢。

cues.en: Not only has Harvard given me an extraordinary honor, but the weeks of fear and nausea I have endured at the thought of giving this commencement address have made me lose weight.
cues.zh: 哈佛不仅给了我一个非凡的荣誉，而且我为想到要发表这个毕业典礼演讲而忍受的数周的恐惧和恶心让我瘦了。

cues.en: A win-win situation.
cues.zh: 雙贏的局面。

cues.en: Now all I have to do is take deep breaths, squint at the red banners, and convince myself that I am at the world's largest Griffin door reunion.
cues.zh: 现在我所要做的就是深呼吸，眯起眼睛看红色的横幅，然后说服自己我正身处世界上最大的格里芬门重聚活动。

cues.en: Delivering a commencement address is a great responsibility.
cues.zh: 发表毕业典礼致辞是一项重大的责任。

cues.en: Or so I thought.
cues.zh: 我曾是这么想的。

cues.en: Until I cast my mind back to my own graduation.
cues.zh: 直到我回想起我自己的毕业典礼。

cues.en: The commencement speaker that day was the distinguished British philosopher, Baroness Mary Warnock.
cues.zh: 那天毕业典礼的演讲者是杰出的英国哲学家玛丽·沃诺克女男爵。

cues.en: Reflecting on her speech has helped me enormously in writing this one.
cues.zh: 回顾她的演讲极大地帮助了我撰写这篇演讲稿。

cues.en: Because it turns out that I can't remember a single word she said.
cues.zh: 因为事实证明，我记不起她说过的任何一个字。

cues.en: This liberating discovery enables me to proceed without any fear that I might inadvertently influence you
cues.zh: 这一令人解脱的发现使我能够继续进行，而不必担心我可能会无意中影响你们

cues.en: to abandon promising careers in business, the law or politics for the giddy delights of becoming a gay wizard.
cues.zh: 放弃在商业、法律或政治领域充满希望的职业，转而追求成为一名同性恋巫师的眩晕般的快乐。

cues.en: You see, if all you remember in years to come is the gay wizard joke,
cues.zh: 你看，如果多年以后你唯一记得的就是那个同性恋巫师的笑话，

cues.en: I've come out ahead of Baroness Mary Warnock.
cues.zh: 我就比玛丽·沃诺克女男爵更胜一筹了。

cues.en: Achievable goals: the first step to self-improvement.
cues.zh: 可实现的目标：自我提升的第一步。

cues.en: Actually, I have wrapped my mind and heart for what I ought to say to you today.
cues.zh: 实际上，我已经为今天该对你们说的话做好了思想和情感上的准备。

cues.en: I have asked myself what I wish I had known at my own graduation, and what important lessons I have learned
cues.zh: 我问自己，在我的毕业典礼上，我希望知道些什么，以及在过去21年里，

cues.en: in the 21 years that have expired between that day and this.
cues.zh: 我学到了哪些重要的教训。

cues.en: I have come up with two answers.
cues.zh: 我得出了两个答案。

cues.en: On this wonderful day when we are gathered together to celebrate your academic success, I have decided to talk to you about the benefits of failure.
cues.zh: 在这个我们齐聚一堂庆祝你们学业成功的伟大日子里，我决定和你们谈谈失败的好处。

cues.en: And as you stand on the threshold of what is sometimes called real life, I want to extol the crucial importance of imagination.
cues.zh: 当你们站在所谓的现实生活门槛上时，我想颂扬想象力的至关重要性。

cues.en: These may seem quixotic or paradoxical choices, but bear with me.
cues.zh: 这些选择可能看起来异想天开或自相矛盾，但请耐心听我说。

cues.en: Looking back at the 21-year-old that I was at graduation, is a slightly uncomfortable experience for the 42-year-old that she has become.
cues.zh: 回望毕业时的21岁的我，对于如今已42岁的她来说，是一种略感不适的体验。

cues.en: Half my lifetime ago, I was striking an uneasy balance between the ambition I had for myself
cues.zh: 半辈子以前，我艰难地在自己雄心壮志与我身边最亲近的人对我的期望之间取得平衡。

cues.en: and what those closest of to me expected of me.
cues.zh: 我艰难地在自己雄心壮志与我身边最亲近的人对我的期望之间取得平衡。

cues.en: I was convinced that the only thing I wanted to do, ever, was write novels.
cues.zh: 我坚信，我一直以来唯一想做的事情就是写小说。

cues.en: However, my parents, both of whom came from impoverished backgrounds and neither of whom had been to college, took the view that my overactive imagination was an amusing personal quirk
cues.zh: 然而，我的父母，他们都来自贫困的家庭，而且两人都没有上过大学，他们认为我过于活跃的想象力是一种有趣的个人怪癖，

cues.en: that would never pay a mortgage or secure a pension.
cues.zh: 永远无法支付房贷或获得养老金。

cues.en: I know the irony strikes with the force of a cartoon anvil now, but.
cues.zh: 我知道现在的讽刺意味就像卡通里的铁砧一样有力，但是。

cues.en: So they hoped that I would take a vocational degree.
cues.zh: 所以他们希望我读一个职业学位。

cues.en: I wanted to study English literature.
cues.zh: 我想学英国文学。

cues.en: A compromise was reached, that in retrospect satisfied nobody,
cues.zh: 达成了一个妥协，但事后看来，没有人满意，

cues.en: and I went up to study modern languages.
cues.zh: 然后我去了学现代语言。

cues.en: Hardly had my parents' car rounded the corner at the end of the road, than I ditched German and scuttled off down the classics corridor.
cues.zh: 我父母的车刚拐过路口，我就放弃了德语，溜进了古典学走廊。

cues.en: I cannot remember telling my parents that I was studying classics; they might well have found out for the first time on graduation day.
cues.zh: 我不记得告诉过父母我在学古典学；他们很可能直到毕业那天才第一次知道。

cues.en: Of all the subjects on this planet, I think they would have been hard put to name one less useful than Greek mythology when it came to securing the keys to an executive bathroom.
cues.zh: 在地球上所有科目中，我认为他们很难说出比希腊神话更有用的科目，当涉及到获得行政浴室的钥匙时。

cues.en: Now I would like to make it clear in parenthesis that I do not blame my parents for their point of view.
cues.zh: 现在我想在括号里说清楚，我不怪我的父母持有他们的观点。

cues.en: There is an expiry date on blaming your parents for steering you in the wrong direction.
cues.zh: 父母在误导你方向这件事上，是有保质期的。

cues.en: The moment you are old enough to take the wheel, responsibility lies with you.
cues.zh: 当你大到可以掌控方向盘的那一刻起，责任就在你身上了。

cues.en: What is more, I cannot criticize my parents for hoping that I would never experience poverty.
cues.zh: 更重要的是，我不能批评我的父母希望我永远不要经历贫困。

cues.en: They had been poor themselves, and I have since been poor.
cues.zh: 他们自己曾经贫穷过，而我后来也贫穷过。

cues.en: And I quite agree with them that it is not an ennobling experience.
cues.zh: 我非常同意他们的看法，贫穷不是一种能使人高尚的经历。

cues.en: Poverty entails fear, and stress, and sometimes depression.
cues.zh: 贫穷意味着恐惧、压力，有时还有抑郁。

cues.en: It means a thousand petty humiliations and hardships.
cues.zh: 它意味着一千种微不足道的羞辱和艰难。

cues.en: Climbing out of poverty by your own efforts, that is something on which to pride yourself.
cues.zh: 靠自己的努力摆脱贫困，那是值得骄傲的事情。

cues.en: But poverty itself is romanticized only by fools.
cues.zh: 但贫穷本身只有傻瓜才会浪漫化。

cues.en: What I feared most for myself at your age was not poverty, but failure.
cues.zh: 在我这个年纪，我最害怕的不是贫穷，而是失败。

cues.en: At your age, in spite of a distinct lack of motivation at university, where I had spent far too long in the coffee bar writing stories,
cues.zh: 在你这个年纪，尽管在大学里明显缺乏动力，我在咖啡馆里花了太长时间写故事，

cues.en: and far too little time at lectures,
